text: Pulse is the living energy every Tribal Power machine runs on. Generators make it, machines spend it, and a **Pulse Cell** lets you carry some in your pocket for tools, spells and travel.

pages.title: Where Pulse lives
text: Pulse is stored energy. A generator such as the Drumheart, the Ley Collector or the Pulse Resonator makes it and keeps it in its own store. A machine spends it while it works, but it can only reach that store through the **lattice**.

Pulse travels only along [Lattice Conductors](lattice_conductor). Anything within **8 blocks** of a conductor is on the lattice: generators, machines, camp hands, relays, totems and [Pulse Cairns](pulse_cairn). Conductors within 8 of each other link into one network, and a machine draws from the generators and cairns on its network. A machine with no conductor in reach starves, even right beside a full drum.

For your first workshop, put one conductor between the drum and the station. Each conductor carries **64 Pulse a second** at first, more as it [ranks](machine_ranks). Machines drain the network's generators first, then its Pulse Cairns. Totems are not for spending: each Resonance Totem holds **250 Pulse** of its own, and that buffer is what keeps its voice.

pages.title: Supply and demand
text: A machine can run for a while from a reserve even when it spends faster than you generate. If it keeps starting and stopping, compare the Pulse it needs with what your generators make, then add generation or build a bigger reserve. Every Pulse figure in this book is for the default settings; a pack can change them, and a machine's readout always shows its real cost.

Totems are not generators. A matching totem gives a station its voice, called **attunement**; it does not make power. Crouch and right-click a machine with this book and it reports power and attunement separately.

steps.caption: A charged Drumheart holds the Pulse you drummed into it.
Right-click it with a Pulse Cell: one use fills the cell as far as the drum holds.
A Pulse Resonator, a voice-craft such as a Wind Harp, or a Pulse Cairn fills a cell the same way, all it can take in one use.
The generator loses what the cell gains. A Ley Collector cannot fill a cell this way.

pages.title: Carrying it
text: A Pulse Cell holds **1,200 Pulse**; a **Greater Pulse Cell** holds **4,800**; a **Grand Pulse Cell** holds **19,200**. Carry charged cells for spells, Spiritgear, charms and travel, which all draw on cells in your inventory.
A cell in your pocket is **not** on the lattice. Workshops and tablet rites still need Pulse from the lattice around them.

To charge a Way Gate or Far Gate, use a cell on its keystone: each use moves up to **100 Pulse** into it, and trips spend that store, not the cell in your pocket. A Gate Drum needs no Pulse at all: its rite opens it.
Use a cell on a camp to pour Pulse into its **2,400** store for the [camp hands](camp_hands); one use moves as much as the camp has room for.
A [Pulse Gauge](pulse_gauge) pointed at a machine that holds Pulse reads how full it is.
